title: GPT-4’s One-Dimensional Mapping of Morality: How the Accuracy of Country-Estimates Depends on Moral Domain

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing GPT-4's country-level estimates of moral opinions across 63 countries against real-world human survey data (World Value Survey and European Value Study) using Pearson correlations and exploratory factor analysis.

Stratifying the 63 evaluated countries by gross national income (GNI) per capita to measure and compare the discrepancy in GPT-4's predictive accuracy of moral opinions between high-income and low-income countries.

Prompting GPT-4 to estimate each country's placement on a liberal-conservative continuum (0 to 100) and correlating these scores with its moral opinion estimates to demonstrate that the model flattens moral complexity into a single political dimension.
